newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Old Mutual still mulling Dow Sentrachem bid.
newsitem.headline: Old Mutual still mulling Dow Sentrachem bid.

text.p: South Africa's Old Mutual, a major shareholder in chemical firm Sentrachem Ltd, said on Thursday that it was still considering whether it would accept the offer by Dow Chemical of the U.S. for Sentrachem.
"At this stage we have not reached a decision yet," said Roddy Sparks, assistant general manager of investments at Old Mutual.

Sparks added that the group, which owns a Sentrachem stake in the "high teens" in percentage terms, had not yet received an official offer document from Dow and was also waiting for the Sentrachem board's decision.
"We will await the decision of the board, but will make our own decision," he said.
However, industry sources said there was a feeling at Old Mutual that the bid was low and that shareholders may be able to get a better deal if they reject the 10.50 rand a share Dow offer.
"It is a bit low...the company is definitely in play now if this bid does not succeed and anything is possible," one source said.

Dow's bid values Sentrachem at 2.074 billion rand ($441 million) and the U.S. firm has already sealed an agreement from Sankorp Ltd, which holds 38.74 percent of Sentrachem, to accept and recommend the offer.
However, Old Mutual's stake is theoretically big enough to block the offer as Dow has said a condition of the bid is that 90 percent of shareholders accept it.
But Dow has also inserted a clause saying it reserves the right to adjust the 90 percent figure at its discretion.
